name: Trap Bar Romanian Deadlift
description: A Romanian deadlift performed with a trap bar (hex bar). The trap bars neutral grip and symmetrical loading reduces torque on the lumbar spine compared to a standard barbell RDL, while still training the hip hinge pattern with an emphasis on glute and hamstring development through a large range of eccentric loading.

execution.starting_position: Stand inside the trap bar with feet hip-width apart, gripping the handles. Bar should be loaded on the floor or start from the top position.
execution.setup_instructions: Load the trap bar. Stand inside it, grip the handles, and stand upright with hips fully extended as the starting position.
steps: Step 1: Keeping the knees soft and spine neutral, hinge at the hips and push them back.
Step 2: Lower the bar along the sides of the thighs, feeling a progressive stretch in the hamstrings.
Step 3: Once a strong hamstring stretch is felt (typically mid-shin), drive the hips forward.
Step 4: Extend the hips fully at the top, squeezing the glutes, and return to the starting position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale and brace before hinging. Exhale on the drive to standing.
common_mistakes: Rounding the lower back at the bottom of the movement
Bending the knees excessively, turning it into a deadlift
safety_considerations: Keep the bar close to your body throughout the movement
Do not hyperextend the lower back at the top
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Lower until a strong hamstring stretch is felt. Full hip extension at the top.
coaching_cues: Push the hips back, not the chest down
Feel the hamstring stretch at the bottom
